title: Endpoint fallback matrix PRD and staged launch checklist
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: PRD to define a deterministic fallback matrix and staged launch checklist for hosted endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Goal: keep customer traffic served during partial capacity degradations while preserving quality and cost targets. The doc specifies fallbacks by model family, fallback triggers (latency, error rate, cost rate), gating heuristics, operational runbook items, and acceptance criteria for canary and global rollout.
acceptance_criteria: All endpoint types have a defined primary model and at least two fallback tiers with compatibility mapping and documented quality expectations
Fallback activation is driven by automated policies (latency p95, error rate, capacity shortage) and can be toggled via Console feature flag
Canary rollout passes quality and stability gates for 72 hours with no regression in quality metrics beyond defined thresholds
Cost impact of fallback activation is measured and does not exceed +25% of baseline per-token cost in worst-case simulated load
SLOs: global latency p95 for chat <= 300ms during normal traffic and <= 600ms while in fallback (for at most 5% of requests), errors < 0.5%
Operational runbook includes automatic rollback triggers, diagnostic links, and owners for each stage
Automated tests validate model compatibility (input/output schema) for each fallback mapping before rollout
launch_checklist: Create fallback matrix entries in model-catalog service and expose mapping via runtime config
Console: add toggle and per-customer override for fallback policy
Write and land integration tests exercising fallbacks for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
Run synthetic load tests that simulate GPU eviction and verify fallback activation and recovery
Observability: add dashboards for fallback activations, per-model quality delta, and cost delta
Define and test canary cohort (1% of traffic across three customers) and schedule 72h monitoring window
Runbook: document rollback steps, emergency model pinning, and contact list for oncall
Security review: confirm KMS and data routing constraints for private customers do not permit cross-tenant fallback models
Notify Sales/Success for customers with strict model pinning or compliance needs
Schedule post-launch 1-week retrospective and quality review cadence (daily first 3 days, then weekly)
fallback_matrix: Chat primary: redwood-chat-v2 (64k context, fp16), fallback-1: redwood-chat-v2-quant (8-bit, p95 latency +35%), fallback-2: open-7b-quant (cost-optim, quality delta measured via eval set)
Completions primary: redwood-gen-2 (fp16), fallback-1: redwood-gen-2-quant (reduced precision), fallback-2: redwood-gen-1 (smaller architecture)
Embeddings primary: redwood-embed-utf8-l32, fallback-1: redwood-embed-lite-dense (lower-dim), fallback-2: open-3k-embed (external OSS) with 'tagged' routing to indicate reduced recall
Rerank primary: rerank-cross-bert-large, fallback-1: rerank-pointwise-tiny (heuristic-supplied scores), fallback-2: deterministic lexical-scoring (BM25) as last-resort
Model mapping rules include input/output schema compatibility, max sequence length checks, side-channel flags for streaming vs non-streaming
fallback_triggers_and_thresholds: Latency trigger: model p95 > configured SLO for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows -> trigger fallback for affected partition
Error-rate trigger: 5xx rate > 0.5% over 5 minutes -> fallback
Capacity trigger: GPU pool utilization > 92% for 2 minutes -> enable cost-tier fallback for best-effort traffic
Quality-safety guard: fallback applies only when eval-simulated quality degradation <= configured threshold (default: embeddings recall drop <= 6%, LM generation BLEU/ROUGE proxy <= 8% delta)
Per-customer override: customer-configured pin prevents fallback to off-hosted or lower-cert models (must be honored and cause routed errors instead)
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Dry-run - configure fallback matrix in staging, run end-to-end integration tests under synthetic evictions
Phase 1: Canary - 1% traffic, 3 customers representing low, medium, high latency profiles. 72h monitoring window. Manual approval required to proceed.
Phase 2: Gradual ramp - increase to 10% over 48h, gating on error rate and quality deltas; collect cost telemetry
Phase 3: Region-wide - enable for non-compliant customers in non-sensitive regions; coordinate with Sales for enterprise customers
Phase 4: Global - enable by default with per-customer opt-outs and final docs published
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: fallback activations by model/pool, customer, region
Metric: quality_delta_per_model (daily) with alert if > configured threshold
Alert: fallback_activation_rate > 2% sustained for 30 minutes -> Severity P1 page
Alert: per-customer fallback activation for > 10% of requests -> notify account manager
Tracing: link fallback decision traces back to original request and runtime kernel selection logs
qa_tests: Integration test: request-response schema validated across primary and every fallback for chat and completions
Load test: simulate GPU pool node loss and verify fallback activation within threshold time
Quality smoke: run canonical prompt set and validate metric deltas against baseline for each fallback
Compatibility test: streaming session resume semantics preserved when switching to fallback (chat long-running)
Embeddings upstream test: verify index recall/latency impact when switching embedding model under query suite
tradeoffs: Cost vs quality: more aggressive fallback reduces cost but increases returned quality variance; thresholds must be tunable per tenant
Observability overhead: increased telemetry and tracing needed to understand fallbacks; adds cost and complexity
Operational complexity: per-customer pinning increases engineering gating logic and can prevent graceful fallback for some enterprise customers
Cross-model fallbacks increase risk of subtle output format differences; we mitigate with schema adapters and automated compatibility tests
decisions: Default global policy will prioritize latency-preserving fallbacks over cost-preserving fallbacks for chat endpoints
Embeddings will have explicit 'recall budget' tiers allowing customers to opt into lower-cost fallbacks with documented expected recall loss
Rerank will fallback to deterministic lexical scoring only as last-resort to avoid silent semantic quality loss
Console feature flag required before any customer-facing rollout; no silent global switch
open_questions: How should we represent fallback-induced provenance to downstream apps that rely on exact model semantics? (metadata header vs response envelope)
What is the acceptable SLT (secondary latency target) for customers on Dedicated vs Hosted tiers during fallback?
Should we expose 'fallback-reason' in success responses to customers by default, or behind an opt-in telemetry flag?
Do we allow cross-region fallback (serve from different region) for non-sensitive workloads, and what data residency implications exist?

notes: We must ensure schema adapters for streaming vs non-streaming outputs to avoid client-side regressions when fallback changes streaming behavior.
Benchmarks should include cold-start and warm cache scenarios; some quantized fallbacks show transient latency spikes on cold starts.
Document expected quality deltas per fallback and keep them versioned in the model-catalog for reference in Console and billing docs.
